t: Minimum Weighted Subgraph With the Required Paths II
o: In a weighted tree, for each query (a, b, c) find the minimum total edge weight of a connected subgraph through which both a and b can reach c. The minimal such subgraph is the Steiner tree of the three terminals, and in a tree it is exactly the union of the three terminal paths; its weight is (d(a,b) + d(a,c) + d(b,c)) / 2, since each edge of the union is counted exactly twice across the three pairwise distances. Example 1, query (2,3,4): d=8,9,7 gives (8+9+7)/2 = 12. So the whole problem reduces to weighted distances, i.e., LCA with depth-weighted prefix sums via binary lifting.
k: Steiner tree of 3 terminals in a tree weighs (d(a,b) + d(a,c) + d(b,c)) / 2.
Binary lifting gives O(log n) LCA per query after O(n log n) preprocessing.

a.n: Approach 1: Binary-lifting LCA with weighted depths
a.i: Root the tree at 0, compute weighted depth and ancestor tables, answer each query with the three pairwise distances combined by the Steiner formula.
s: Build adjacency; BFS/DFS to get parent, unweighted depth, weighted depth.
Per query compute lca of each pair and return (d_ab + d_ac + d_bc) / 2.
a.t: O((n + q) log n) — lifting-table build plus three O(log n) LCA calls per query
a.sp: O(n log n) for the ancestor table

w: Recognizing the Steiner-tree-in-a-tree formula is the entire difficulty; after that it is boilerplate LCA. Distances fit in 64-bit (path weight <= 1e4 * 1e5 = 1e9, sums to 3e9). Pitfall: rooting consistently and dividing by 2 only at the end. Follow-up: extend to more terminals (virtual trees / auxiliary-tree construction) or handle edge updates with LCT.
